place.t_kin_village: a village where your kin live
ev.t_road_robbers.title: Ambush on the Road
ev.t_road_robbers.text: On an empty stretch of road five men step out of the bushes with clubs and knives. One grabs your mule's bridle, another is already rummaging through your packs. Their leader, a scar running down his cheek, smiles almost kindly: “Your purse, and go in peace.”
ev.t_road_robbers.text.rome: On a deserted stretch of road between two roadside tombs, five men climb over a wall with clubs and knives — runaway slaves or ruined shepherds, there's no telling. Their leader, a scar running down his cheek, smiles almost kindly: “Your purse, and go in peace.”
ev.t_road_robbers.text.egypt: The caravan fell behind, and on the empty road between villages five men on donkeys surround you, armed with sticks and sickles. Their leader, a scar running down his cheek, smiles almost kindly: “Your purse, and go in peace.”
ev.t_road_robbers.hand_over.ok: They took your purse, your cloak, even your sandals. You limped home barefoot, counting every stone and every lost coin.
ev.t_road_robbers.fight.success: You grabbed a cart pole and knocked the first one flat. The rest scattered, but the leader looked back as he ran and memorized your face. You memorized his.
ev.t_road_robbers.fight.failure: There were too many. You woke in a ditch with a cracked head and no money — and, for some reason, the mule.
ev.t_road_robbers.bluff: Say soldiers are right behind you
ev.t_road_robbers.bluff.success: You waved so confidently at the dust beyond the bend that the robbers exchanged looks and melted into the brush. The dust turned out to be a flock of sheep.
ev.t_road_robbers.bluff.failure: The leader laughed. “Soldiers? Out here?” For the lie they took twice as much — your purse and a beating.
ev.t_road_robbers.flee.success: You ran until your lungs gave out. The packs are gone, but the purse inside your tunic is safe.
ev.t_road_robbers.flee.failure: One of them caught you at a stream. The purse followed the packs, and the bruises stayed with you.
ev.t_robbers_caught.title: The Gang Is Caught
ev.t_robbers_caught.text: The robbers from the road have been caught. You're summoned to identify them and reclaim what's left of the loot. Among the bound men is a boy of thirteen who held your mule that day. He looks at you and says nothing.
ev.t_robbers_caught.identify.ok: You pointed at each of them. Some of your goods came back, and the trial was short. You lay awake that night — but justice is justice.
ev.t_robbers_caught.spare_boy.ok: The boy was let go. A month later he turned up at your door asking for work — and he's followed you like a shadow ever since.
ev.t_night_burglary.title: The Hole in the Wall
ev.t_night_burglary.text: A draft wakes you: there's a gaping hole in the storeroom wall, and the chest with your savings for a rainy day is gone. Hurried footsteps still echo down the street. Years of saving are in someone else's hands.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.athens: A draft wakes you: “wall-diggers” have tunneled through the mud-brick wall of your storeroom, and the chest with your savings for a rainy day is gone. Hurried footsteps still echo down the street. Years of saving are in someone else's hands.
ev.t_night_burglary.chase.success: You caught up with them in an alley: the chest is heavy and thieves aren't athletes. They dropped it and fled with only a handful of coins.
ev.t_night_burglary.chase.failure: In the dark you tripped over a barrel and smashed your knee. The footsteps faded, and with them everything you'd saved.
ev.t_night_burglary.curse: Pay for a curse on the thief
ev.t_night_burglary.curse.ok: A wise woman scratched it onto a lead tablet — “May whoever took it neither sleep nor eat until it is returned” — and dropped it down a well. It hasn't brought the money back, but you sleep better.
ev.t_night_burglary.accuse.success: You were right: the chest turned up at a fence your neighbor did business with. Nearly all of it came back.
ev.t_night_burglary.accuse.failure: The suspicion was empty, the offense was real. No money — and a neighbor who now hates you.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok: You patched the wall and decided: from now on your money stays in a temple, under the eyes of gods and priests. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_burglar_returns.title: The Thief Pays Back
ev.t_burglar_returns.text: In the morning there was a pouch of coins on your doorstep and a note in a clumsy hand: “Lift the curse. I can't take any more.” The tablet in the well did its work.
ev.t_pirates.title: Pirates
ev.t_pirates.text: On the second day at sea two light galleys shot out from behind a headland. Within the hour Cilician pirates owned the deck. The passengers were herded to the stern while the pirates sized them up: who would fetch a ransom, and who was easier to sell at the slave market on Delos.
ev.t_pirates.ransom.success: The letter arrived, and your family raised the money by selling nearly everything. You were put ashore alive, penniless — and free.
ev.t_pirates.ransom.failure: The ransom didn't come in time. You were taken to Delos and sold like a bale of wool. Now you have a master.
ev.t_pirates.boast.success: You laughed at them, recited poetry at them, and promised to come back one day with a fleet. The pirates decided you were someone important, took a modest ransom and let you go with honor.
ev.t_pirates.boast.failure: Your nerve didn't impress them. “Sharp tongues sell well to rhetoric schools,” said the captain, and on Delos you were the first to go.
ev.t_pirates.escape.success: On a moonless night you slipped overboard and reached the shore clinging to an empty wineskin. Fishermen found you on the sand at dawn — without a coin, but free.
ev.t_pirates.escape.failure: They spotted you and fished you out with boathooks. Runaways aren't ransomed — they're sold. Within a week you had a master.
ev.t_pirates.join.ok: The captain liked your strength and gave you an oar and a share of the plunder. There's no road back to an honest life now — not for a while.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.title: A Face from Home
ev.t_pirates_recognized.text: In the market a merchant stares at you — and goes pale. “You're from our town! I knew your father!” You were born free, kidnapped by pirates, and now there's someone who can swear to it.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.plead: Beg him to buy your freedom
ev.t_pirates_recognized.plead.ok: The merchant paid your master and took you home. You're free, but you owe him a great deal — and you'll be paying it back for years.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.sue.success: The merchant swore before the judge that he'd known you since childhood. A free person kidnapped can't be held as a slave: your master had to let you go.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.sue.failure: Your master brought witnesses of his own, and the court didn't believe one merchant. At home a beating and harder work were waiting.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.title: A Fleet on the Horizon
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.text: A Roman fleet is sweeping the sea from coast to coast, and pirate nests are burning one after another. Their commander has proclaimed: those who surrender will get land and pardon; the rest will share the fate of the captured.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.surrender.ok: You laid down your weapons. They gave you a plot in a quiet valley far from the sea. Hands used to an oar are learning to hold a plow.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.keep_raiding.success: Your galley slipped past the Roman ships with rich plunder. You got away and vanished into a port town with a full purse.
ev.t_pirate_amnesty.keep_raiding.failure: The Romans caught you off a headland. You were pulled wounded from the water — and the captured pirate became a slave.
ev.t_shipwreck.title: Shipwreck
ev.t_shipwreck.text: The storm struck at night. The mast snapped, the ship heeled over, and water poured into the hold. The cargo is going down, people are screaming, and toward the shore — are those lights, or stars?
ev.t_shipwreck.vow: Pray to the gods and make a vow
ev.t_shipwreck.vow.success: You swore an offering if you lived — and a wave threw you onto a sandbar right at the feet of fishermen. Now the vow must be kept.
ev.t_shipwreck.vow.failure: The gods heard, but took their time: you drifted two days on a broken spar. You survived — battered, with a vow on your heart.
ev.t_shipwreck.help.success: You pulled three people out of the water, among them a wealthy merchant. He swore he'd never forget that night — and he seemed to mean it.
ev.t_shipwreck.help.failure: You couldn't hold on to the last one, and you swallowed seawater and smashed your arm against the hull. You lived by a miracle.
ev.t_shipwreck.swim.success: The lights were a fishing village. You crawled ashore before dawn, shaking and laughing at being alive.
ev.t_shipwreck.swim.failure: The current dragged you away from shore all night. You were picked up half-dead, and your health has never been the same.
ev.t_shipwreck.strongbox.success: You hauled the chest onto a piece of mast and didn't let go until you reached land. The cargo is lost, but the money is with you.
ev.t_shipwreck.strongbox.failure: The chest dragged you under. You let go at the last moment — no money, but alive.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.title: The Vow
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.text: You dreamed of the sea again, and a voice reminded you: you promised an offering for your rescue. At the temple the priest nodded as if he'd been expecting you. “The gods are patient, but they have long memories.”
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.pay.ok: You ordered a little silver ship and a sacrifice for the whole quarter. It felt like shedding a sodden cloak.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.tablet.ok: The tablet shows a sinking ship and you clinging to a spar. Modest but honest — the temple has hundreds like it.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.forget.ok: You decided you swam out on your own. The neighbors shake their heads, and you've avoided the sea ever since.
ev.t_buried_treasure.title: Buried Treasure
ev.t_buried_treasure.text: The plow clanks against something hard. Under the clods is a clay pot full of heavy old coins, green with age. Someone buried them during a long-ago war and never came back. Across the boundary stone, your neighbor is watching.
ev.t_buried_treasure.report: Report the find to the authorities
ev.t_buried_treasure.report.ok: The treasure was divided according to the law, and your share is still more than you've seen in your whole life. The whole district talks about your honesty.
ev.t_buried_treasure.keep.ok: You reburied the pot under the hearth and spend a little at a time so no one notices. Only your neighbor has become suspiciously friendly.
ev.t_buried_treasure.temple.ok: The priests accepted the gift gratefully and set aside a small share for you. The earth gave the gods what wasn't hers — so the village says.
ev.t_buried_treasure.share.ok: You divided the coins right there on the boundary. Now you have money — and someone who keeps the same secret.
ev.t_treasure_informer.title: Informed On
ev.t_treasure_informer.text: Someone has informed on you about the treasure. An official arrives with a scribe and guards. “Concealing a find is a crime. Where are the coins?”
ev.t_treasure_informer.pay: Hand it over and pay the fine
ev.t_treasure_informer.pay.ok: You had to give up almost everything left, and more besides. The wealth went as fast as it came.
ev.t_treasure_informer.deny.success: They found nothing under the hearth — you'd moved the pot long ago. The official left empty-handed, but the rumors stayed.
ev.t_treasure_informer.deny.failure: They found the pot, and for lying the fine was doubled. The neighbors greet you through clenched teeth now.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.title: A Letter About an Inheritance
ev.t_distant_inheritance.text: A messenger brings a sealed letter: in a distant city your mother's cousin has died childless — a man you never met. His will leaves everything to you: house, workshop, slaves. And debts, which no one can put a number to.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.text.rome: A messenger brings a will sealed by seven witnesses: in a distant city your mother's cousin has died childless. Everything is yours — on condition that you take his name and honor his tomb. And debts, which no one can put a number to.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.accept.success: The debts were small and the house is in the best part of town. Suddenly you're a person of means.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.accept.failure: The creditors descended like gulls. The debts ate the inheritance, and you had to pay the rest out of your own pocket.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.sell_rights: Sell your claim to a speculator
ev.t_distant_inheritance.sell_rights.ok: A shrewd speculator paid good money for the claim. How much he made himself, you'd rather not know.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.give_away: Give it to his poor relatives
ev.t_distant_inheritance.give_away.ok: You renounced it in favor of his brother's widow and her children. She wept and kissed your hands, and the story spread through two cities.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.title: A Second Will
ev.t_inheritance_contest.text: A distant cousin of the deceased has turned up with another will — supposedly a later one. The seals look suspiciously fresh, and the witnesses suspiciously well fed.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.court.success: The judge noticed the wax on the seals still smelled of the beehive. The forgery was thrown out; the inheritance is yours.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.court.failure: The court believed the witnesses. Half the inheritance went to the impostor, and you made an enemy.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.settle: Split it to avoid a lawsuit
ev.t_inheritance_contest.settle.ok: You divided the property before witnesses. Galling, but peaceful.
ev.t_earthquake.title: Earthquake
ev.t_earthquake.text: At dawn the ground roared and heaved. Walls cracked, roof tiles rained into the street, and a knocked-over brazier started a fire somewhere. A scream comes from under the rubble of the house next door.
ev.t_earthquake.text.rome: At dawn the ground roared and heaved, like the time Campania shook. Walls cracked, roof tiles rained into the street, and a knocked-over brazier started a fire somewhere. A scream comes from under the rubble of the house next door.
ev.t_earthquake.text.egypt: At dawn the ground roared and shuddered — in Egypt, where it rarely happens, people cry out that the gods are angry. Mud-brick walls crumble, and a scream comes from under the rubble of the house next door.
ev.t_earthquake.dig.success: With bare hands you dug out your neighbor and his children. That family will remember you in their prayers for the rest of their lives.
ev.t_earthquake.dig.failure: The wall came down again and pinned your leg. Others pulled the neighbor out, and you limped for a long time.
ev.t_earthquake.save_goods.ok: You got everything valuable out before the looters came. The neighbors remember who dug through rubble and who dug through their own chests.
ev.t_earthquake.run_free.success: In the dust and screaming nobody saw you slip out of the gate. They'll count you among the dead under the rubble — the best gift fate could give.
ev.t_earthquake.run_free.failure: You were seized at the city gate. Your master decided you'd tried to profit from disaster — and he was right.
ev.t_earthquake.leave.ok: You gathered what survived and went to your kin. Let the earth shake without you.
ev.t_patron_falls.title: The Patron Falls
ev.t_patron_falls.text: {npc}, your patron, has fallen from grace overnight: accusation, trial, confiscation. Yesterday petitioners crowded {g=npc_sex:his|her} door; today the street is empty. Everyone connected with {g=npc_sex:him|her} is under suspicion — you included.
ev.t_patron_falls.text.rome: {npc}, your patron, has fallen out of favor with the powerful overnight: accusation, trial, confiscation. Yesterday clients crowded {g=npc_sex:his|her} door at dawn; today the street is empty. Everyone connected with {g=npc_sex:him|her} is under suspicion — you included.
ev.t_patron_falls.text.egypt: {npc}, your patron, has lost the favor of the royal court in Alexandria overnight: accusation, confiscation, guards at the door. Everyone connected with {g=npc_sex:him|her} is under suspicion — you included.
ev.t_patron_falls.stand.success: You brought {g=npc_sex:him|her} food and spoke up when others kept silent. The storm passed, and {npc} won't forget who stood by.
ev.t_patron_falls.stand.failure: Loyalty cost dearly: you were dragged in for questioning and part of your property was seized. {npc} went into exile, and the tie was cut.
ev.t_patron_falls.denounce.ok: Your testimony helped the prosecution and you were generously rewarded. But in the street people whisper a word behind your back that's worse than any curse.
ev.t_patron_falls.vanish.ok: You went to your kin, abandoning half your affairs. No one touched you — they simply forgot you.
ev.t_patron_returns.title: Back from Exile
ev.t_patron_returns.text: Your old patron has returned: the charges dropped, part of the property restored. The first person he sent for was you. “You alone didn't turn away. One doesn't forget that.” In his hands is a heavy purse.
ev.t_denounce_shame.title: The Son Remembers
ev.t_denounce_shame.text: The son of the man you once testified against has grown up. In the middle of the market, loudly, he reminded everyone how you paid for your comfort. Now you have an enemy for life.
ev.t_speech_fame.title: The Voice of the Crowd
ev.t_speech_fame.text: You never meant to speak — you just couldn't stand it when the crowd started slandering an honest man. The words came on their own; people laughed at first, then fell silent, then roared. By morning there were people waiting at your door.
ev.t_speech_fame.text.athens: On the Pnyx you never meant to speak — you just couldn't stand it when they started slandering an honest man. The words came on their own; the Assembly laughed at first, then fell silent, then roared. By morning there were people waiting at your door.
ev.t_speech_fame.politics.success: You threw banquets, spoke on every corner — and became a man to be reckoned with. The powerful now seek your friendship.
ev.t_speech_fame.politics.failure: The second speech was worse than the first; the third was jeered. The money for banquets is gone, and the fame was shorter than a festival.
ev.t_speech_fame.mouthpiece.ok: A rich man pays you to say his words. He pays well. The words do sometimes stick in your throat.
ev.t_speech_fame.back_to_work: Go back to your own work
ev.t_speech_fame.back_to_work.ok: You waved off the offers. The fame faded in a month; your neighbors' respect remained.
ev.t_fame_enemies.title: Old Words
ev.t_fame_enemies.text: The man you once mocked in a speech hasn't forgotten. Now he's rich, and he's taken you to court — for slander and anything else he could think of.
ev.t_fame_enemies.defend.success: You made the crowd laugh again — at him, again. The suit was dismissed and your fame flared up anew.
ev.t_fame_enemies.defend.failure: This time the words didn't come. The court fined you, and this time they laughed at you.
ev.t_fame_enemies.pay_off.ok: He took the money and dropped the suit. He won — but at least quietly.
ev.t_friend_betrays.title: The Surety
ev.t_friend_betrays.text: You stood surety for {npc} when {g=npc_sex:he|she} needed a large loan. Now {npc} has vanished with the money, and the lender is at your door with a contract where your name is written right beside {g=npc_sex:his|hers}.
ev.t_friend_betrays.pay.ok: You gave up half of everything you had. The lender left satisfied, and you no longer speak the name {npc}.
ev.t_friend_betrays.chase.success: You found the runaway at the quay, luggage already on the gangplank. Nearly all the money came back. The friendship didn't.
ev.t_friend_betrays.chase.failure: The ship left an hour before you arrived. The journey cost plenty, and the debt is still yours.
ev.t_friend_betrays.deny.success: No witnesses turned up and the court left you alone. But people remember that you went back on your word.
ev.t_friend_betrays.deny.failure: The lender produced two witnesses. You paid with interest — and got a liar's name into the bargain.
ev.t_friend_returns.title: The Prodigal Debtor
ev.t_friend_returns.text: The one you stood surety for has come back — gray-haired, in an expensive cloak. He stands at your door holding a purse and can't raise his eyes. “I made my fortune overseas. Here's everything I owe you, and more.”
ev.t_friend_returns.take.ok: You counted the coins in front of him. Every one. The debt is closed — and nothing more.
ev.t_friend_returns.forgive.ok: You sat until morning over wine, remembering your youth. Not every friendship can be saved, but this one was.
ev.t_friend_returns.drive_away.ok: You shut the door without taking a single coin. Pride is capital too.
ev.t_uncover_crime.title: Someone Else's Secret
ev.t_uncover_crime.text: Late one evening you happen to see the steward carrying out sacks of the master's grain and rewriting the accounts. He looks up — and realizes you saw everything. “Surely we can come to an arrangement,” he says quietly.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report.success: The owner checked the accounts and threw the thief out. You were rewarded and trusted more than ever.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report.failure: The steward got there first: you were blamed for the theft. You had to pay and explain yourself, and now you have an enemy.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report_master.success: The master counted the sacks himself and went pale. The thief was sold to the quarries, and the master took notice of you — perhaps more notice than you think.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report_master.failure: The master believed the steward, not a slave. You were flogged for slander, and the steward now watches you like a wolf.
ev.t_uncover_crime.blackmail: Take a share for your silence
ev.t_uncover_crime.blackmail.ok: Now once a month he silently slips you a pouch of coins. You both know it won't last forever.
ev.t_uncover_crime.silent.ok: You pretended you saw nothing. Only now it's hard to look him in the eye — or yourself.
ev.t_blackmail_turns.title: The Thief Rises
ev.t_blackmail_turns.text: The steward you kept quiet about for years has bought his freedom, grown rich and made friends. Now he wants the witness gone. “Give back everything you took — or you'll regret it.”
ev.t_blackmail_turns.pay.ok: You gave back all of it and more. The old secret has finally stopped being worth money.
ev.t_blackmail_turns.expose.success: The old accounts survived, and the court believed them. The thief was convicted and you were rewarded as a witness.
ev.t_blackmail_turns.expose.failure: He had friends among the judges. You were beaten in an alley, and the city calls you an extortionist.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.title: Your {g=npc_sex:Son|Daughter} Is Missing
ev.t_child_kidnapped.text: {npc} didn't come home from the market. A fisherman saw a child being led to a slave trader's ship moored at the far quay. The ship sails with the evening wind.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.chase.success: You stormed up the gangplank with a scream you wouldn't have recognized as your own. The traders didn't want trouble: {npc} is home again and asleep, holding your hand.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.chase.failure: The ship was already pulling away. You ran along the quay until it vanished into the dusk. You never saw {g=npc_sex:him|her} again.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.ransom.success: The go-between took the money, and within the hour {npc} was in your arms. You walked home in silence and didn't let go for a moment.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.ransom.failure: The go-between took the money and disappeared. The ship sailed with the evening wind.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.magistrate.success: The watch closed the harbor and searched the ship. {npc} was in the hold among other people's children — terrified, but alive.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.magistrate.failure: While the watchmen were gathering, the ship slipped away. The official spread his hands: the sea is large.
ev.t_lost_child_news.title: News from Afar
ev.t_lost_child_news.text: Many years later a letter comes from a distant city. The child stolen from you is alive: a kind master set them free, and they have a family and a trade of their own. At the end, in an unpracticed hand: “I remember your voice.”
ev.t_lost_child_news.send_money.ok: You sent a purse with a merchant, along with a letter it took you three nights to write. For the first time in years, you breathe easier.
ev.t_lost_child_news.go_see.ok: The journey was long. You didn't recognize each other at first — and then you talked until dawn.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.title: You Are Being Sold
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. A contractor who buys people for the hardest labor has already inspected you — no one comes back from there young. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text.athens: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. A contractor from the Laurion silver mines has already inspected you — no one comes back from there young. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text.rome: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. The steward of a vast estate, where slaves work in chains and sleep in a cellar, has already inspected you. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text.egypt: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. A contractor for the royal quarries in the eastern desert has already inspected you — no one comes back from there young. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.plead: Throw yourself at your master's feet
ev.t_slave_sold_away.plead.success: Your master remembered your years of service and sold a mule instead. You stay — for now.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.plead.failure: Your master turned away. In the morning you were led off in a column, and life became twice as hard.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.show_skill: Show the buyers what you can do
ev.t_slave_sold_away.show_skill.ok: You read the goods list aloud and tallied it in your head. The steward of a rich household, who'd come for a cook, outbid the contractor — and took you to the city instead of the mines.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.run.success: You climbed the wall and followed a streambed so the dogs would lose the scent. Somewhere ahead lie a new name and a free life.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.run.failure: The dogs found you by morning. For a runaway: a brand, and the hardest work there is.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.accept.ok: You went without a word. The work is brutal, but you endure — and the overseers are starting to notice.
ev.t_overseer_chance.title: The Whip in Your Hand
ev.t_overseer_chance.text: The old overseer has died, and the steward picked you. “You're tough and you don't whine. You'll watch the others.” Better food, lighter work — but you'll have to raise the whip against your own.
ev.t_overseer_chance.take.ok: Now you have a corner of your own and an extra bowl of stew. And looks you can't hide from.
ev.t_overseer_chance.refuse.ok: The steward shrugged and chose someone else. The work stays the same, but the others in the barracks now share their last crust with you.
ev.t_slave_born_free.title: You Were Born Free
ev.t_slave_born_free.text: A dying old slave woman called you over one night and whispered: you were stolen as a baby from a free family in the next town; she remembers your father's name and the street. Which means that by law you shouldn't be a slave at all.
ev.t_slave_born_free.sue.success: A free man agreed to plead your cause, and old witnesses confirmed the story. The court declared you freeborn.
ev.t_slave_born_free.sue.failure: Your master called it an old woman's ravings, and the court agreed. Now he looks at you as an enemy.
ev.t_slave_born_free.search_family: Secretly send word to the family
ev.t_slave_born_free.search_family.ok: You begged a mule driver to carry the old woman's words to the next town. Now all you can do is wait.
ev.t_slave_born_free.silent.ok: You buried the old woman and her secret with her. But at night you think about an unknown street in the next town.
ev.t_born_free_family.title: A Brother
ev.t_born_free_family.text: A stranger with your eyes stands at the gate. “Mother died still waiting for you,” he says. “I've saved enough to buy you out. Let's go home.”
ev.t_born_free_family.go.ok: Your master took the money, and you walked out of the gate free. You have a brother, a home, and the name you were given at birth.
ev.t_born_free_family.stay.ok: Your people are here — the ones you've shared bread and grief with. Your brother left in tears, promising to come back.
ev.t_slave_saves.title: A Child in the River
ev.t_slave_saves.text: The master's son slipped on the jetty and fell into the river. The current is carrying him fast toward a whirlpool; the nurse is screaming, and everyone else is frozen on the bank.
ev.t_slave_saves.rush.success: You dragged the boy ashore alive. The master wept as he held his son, and a week later, before witnesses, he declared you free.
ev.t_slave_saves.rush.failure: A fisherman in a boat pulled the boy out, and the current smashed you against the rocks. The master is grateful, but gave you no freedom.
ev.t_slave_saves.call_help.ok: The boatmen pulled the boy out. The master noticed you kept your head — and that's all.
ev.t_slave_saves.use_chaos.success: Everyone was watching the river, and you slipped into the reeds and never came back. They say the boy was saved. They're still looking for you.
ev.t_slave_saves.use_chaos.failure: You were caught before sunset. A runaway who left a child to drown — the master won't forgive that.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.title: Two Roads to Freedom
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.text: The freedman potter across the street would give all his savings to buy you and make you his wife. And your master, a widower, hinted yesterday that he'd free you himself — if you became his wife. You have to answer both.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.potter.success: Your master took the money without haggling. You left his house free and that same evening entered the potter's house as its mistress.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.potter.failure: Your master took offense and sold you to an estate outside the city. The potter kept coming to the gate for a long time.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.master.ok: He freed you before witnesses and called you his wife. Yesterday's kitchen companions bow to you now — and whisper behind your back.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.refuse.ok: You won't buy freedom at the price of yourself. The master scowls, the potter waits, and you save every coin on your own.
ev.t_master_heirs.title: Children of the First Marriage
ev.t_master_heirs.text: Your husband's grown children by his first wife declare that you bewitched their father for his money. They demand that a former slave know her place — and give back everything she got.
ev.t_master_heirs.court.success: Your husband came to court himself and said he chose you of his own free will. The suit was dismissed and your share set down in writing.
ev.t_master_heirs.court.failure: The court sided with the children. You had to give up half the property, and your name was dragged through the whole city.
ev.t_master_heirs.concede: Give up a share for peace
ev.t_master_heirs.concede.ok: You gave them the estate outside the city. The house is quieter, if not warmer.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.title: The Dowry
ev.t_dowry_divorce.text: You've found out that {npc} has squandered your dowry — on dice, debts and empty schemes. Your father and brothers put it plainly: divorce, and demand your property back before it's too late. The law is on your side, but courts are slow.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.divorce.success: You returned to your father's house with your dowry and your head held high. Free, with money — and with new thoughts about the future.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.divorce.failure: The divorce went through, but only a fraction came back. The neighbor women whisper that it was all your own fault.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.take_purse: Take the purse into your own hands
ev.t_dowry_divorce.take_purse.ok: The key to the strongbox now hangs at your belt. Your husband doesn't like it, but for the first time in years the household makes ends meet.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.endure: Endure it for peace at home
ev.t_dowry_divorce.endure.ok: You said nothing. {npc} promised to mend {g=npc_sex:his|her} ways — and you very much want to believe it.
ev.t_second_marriage.title: New Suitors
ev.t_second_marriage.text: A divorced woman with a dowry is a fine match, and the matchmakers soon come calling. An elderly, wealthy widower is asking for your hand — and so is a young craftsman of modest means you've had your eye on for a while.
ev.t_second_marriage.rich_widower.ok: A big house, a quiet life, a husband who doesn't interfere. Not love — but not a mistake either.
ev.t_second_marriage.for_love.ok: Less money, more laughter. For the first time you're marrying by your own choice, not by your fathers' agreement.
ev.t_second_marriage.stay_free.ok: You're mistress of your dowry and your days. Lonely sometimes — but no one will squander what's yours again.
ev.t_midwife_accused.title: Accused of Poisoning
ev.t_midwife_accused.text: A woman from a rich household died in childbirth, though you did everything you could. Her family is shouting up and down the street that your herbs are poison and you're a witch. Accusations like that end in court — and sometimes worse.
ev.t_midwife_accused.defend: Call the women you've helped as witnesses
ev.t_midwife_accused.defend.success: Twenty women came to court with children in their arms — every one of them delivered by you. The judges fell silent and the accusers left.
ev.t_midwife_accused.defend.failure: The witnesses were too frightened to come. You were fined, your name disgraced, and you'll long remember the stone thrown from the crowd.
ev.t_midwife_accused.flee.ok: You left at night with nothing but your bag of herbs. There are women giving birth in your kin's village too — and no one there knows your story.
ev.t_midwife_accused.altar: Take refuge at an altar and swear by the gods
ev.t_midwife_accused.altar.success: You swore a terrible oath at the altar, and the priests spoke up for you. The dead woman's family backed down — no one argues with the gods.
ev.t_midwife_accused.altar.failure: They heard the oath but didn't believe it. The disgrace stayed, and your patients now go to someone else.
ev.t_widowhood.title: Widowhood
ev.t_widowhood.text: {npc} died suddenly, within three days. After the funeral you're alone with the household, debts you never knew about, and a crowd at the door: some have come for money, others to propose.
ev.t_widowhood.run_business: Take the business into your own hands
ev.t_widowhood.run_business.success: You untangled the accounts, sacked a dishonest worker and went to the suppliers yourself. A year later the business earns more than it did under your husband.
ev.t_widowhood.run_business.failure: Debtors won't pay, workers steal, and merchants won't deal with a woman. You had to sell half of everything.
ev.t_widowhood.remarry.ok: Your husband's partner proposed marriage as a business deal. Debts settled, house saved — and feelings may come in time.
ev.t_widowhood.return_home: Go back to your parents' house
ev.t_widowhood.return_home.ok: You handed the household over to the creditors and went back to your own people. Poorer — but among familiar voices.
ev.t_poetess.title: Verses
ev.t_poetess.text: The verses you wrote for a friend's wedding are being sung all over the city. A wealthy connoisseur invites you to recite at his banquets, and your family is horrified: a respectable woman shouldn't have her name on everyone's lips.
ev.t_poetess.publish.success: Your verses are copied onto papyrus and learned by heart. The best houses invite you, and even your family is proud now — out loud.
ev.t_poetess.publish.failure: The gossip was louder than the poems. People say all sorts of things about you, and not one word is about rhyme.
ev.t_poetess.under_his_name: Let your brother read them as his own
ev.t_poetess.under_his_name.ok: Your brother got the fame and the gifts; you got a share of the money and a quiet bitterness. At least he shares honestly.
ev.t_poetess.burn.ok: The hearth fire made short work of the papyrus. The lines still sound in your head, but soon they'll fade too.
ev.t_poems_live_on.title: Strangers' Voices
ev.t_poems_live_on.text: In a distant port you heard sailors you'd never met singing your verses — with mistakes, in their own way, but yours. None of them knows who wrote them. And somehow that's the most beautiful part.
ev.t_youth_teacher.title: The Wandering Teacher
ev.t_youth_teacher.text: A wandering teacher — gray-haired, in worn sandals, with a bag of scrolls — watched you argue with a merchant and invited you to come with him: to study, copy books, see the world. But your hands are needed at home, and your father has no love for philosophers.
ev.t_youth_teacher.ask_blessing.success: Your father was silent a long time, then said, “Just don't become one of those windbags.” Your mother packed a bundle, and at dawn you left with the teacher.
ev.t_youth_teacher.ask_blessing.failure: Your father forbade you even to think of it. The teacher left alone, and you watched the road for a long time.
ev.t_youth_teacher.run_off: Slip away at night without asking
ev.t_youth_teacher.run_off.ok: You caught up with the teacher at the city gate. Ahead: scrolls, arguments and new cities. Behind: a home where you won't soon be forgiven.
ev.t_youth_teacher.stay.ok: You walked the teacher to the crossroads. Your father clapped you on the shoulder like a grown-up for the first time.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.title: The Teacher's Legacy
ev.t_teacher_legacy.text: Your old teacher has died and left you everything he had: a chest of scrolls, a threadbare cloak, and a dozen pupils who are now looking at you.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.open_school: Open a school of your own
ev.t_teacher_legacy.open_school.ok: You hung a sign over the door and started teaching. The pay is small, but boys from the neighboring quarters come to you and no one else.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.sell_library.ok: A book collector paid good money for the scrolls. The teacher would probably have winced — or perhaps laughed.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.donate: Give the scrolls to a temple library
ev.t_teacher_legacy.donate.ok: Now many people read his books, and a tablet with his name stands on the shelf. Yours is there too, in smaller letters.
ev.t_plunder_share.title: The Fallen City
ev.t_plunder_share.text: The city has fallen after a long siege, and the commander has allowed plunder until morning. In the cellar of a rich house you find a woman with two children, clutching a casket to her chest. On the hill a temple is burning, and soldiers are already hauling out gold.
ev.t_plunder_share.take_casket.ok: You took the casket and left without looking back. There was gold in it. And that woman's eyes, which won't leave your memory.
ev.t_plunder_share.spare: Lead the family out of the city
ev.t_plunder_share.spare.ok: You led them through a breach in the wall to an olive grove. The woman pressed a ring into your hand and said something in her own language. The boy watched you go for a long time.
ev.t_plunder_share.loot_temple.ok: You carried a golden bowl and a fistful of coins out of the temple. Wealth for life. They say foreign gods have long memories too.
ev.t_spared_family.title: The Boy from the Cellar
ev.t_spared_family.text: A young merchant came to your door and asked for you by name. He is the boy from the cellar in the fallen city. “Mother told me to find you,” he said. “She died blessing you.” He's carrying a purse and gifts.
ev.t_loot_curse.title: The Wrath of Foreign Gods
ev.t_loot_curse.text: Ever since you carried gold out of that temple, you dream of a burning hill. Misfortune follows misfortune, and the soothsayer put it bluntly: “The gods of that city want what is theirs.”
ev.t_loot_curse.return_gold: Give the gold to a temple
ev.t_loot_curse.return_gold.ok: You gave most of the plunder to a temple. The dreams stopped, as if washed away by rain.
ev.t_loot_curse.sacrifice.ok: You made sacrifices and hung up amulets. It's a little easier — or so it seems.
ev.t_loot_curse.ignore.ok: You sent the soothsayer away. The dreams didn't stop, and your health began to fail too.
ev.t_grain_hoard.title: The Hungry Year
ev.t_grain_hoard.text: The harvest failed, the grain ships are late, and the price of bread has tripled. And your granaries are full. At the gate stand both speculators with fat purses and the hungry with empty baskets.
ev.t_grain_hoard.hoard: Hold the grain and sell high
ev.t_grain_hoard.hoard.success: You sold the grain at the highest price the city has ever seen. Your wealth grows, and someone writes unkind things about you in charcoal on the walls.
ev.t_grain_hoard.hoard.failure: A mob broke down the granary gates. Some of the grain was carried off, the rest burned, and you were nearly killed.
ev.t_grain_hoard.fair.ok: You sold at the old price until the grain ran out. A modest profit, but the city calls you an honest man.
ev.t_grain_hoard.donate.ok: You opened your granaries and handed out bread for a whole week. A city doesn't forget that.
ev.t_honorary_decree.title: An Honorary Decree
ev.t_honorary_decree.text: The city council has voted in your honor: to carve the decree in stone, set up your statue by the temple, and give you a seat of honor at festivals. Beneath the statue is an inscription about that hungry year.
ev.t_big_commission.title: The Big Commission
ev.t_big_commission.text: A temple is looking for a workshop for an enormous commission — two years of work that will either make your name or ruin you. To take it on, you'll need to borrow for materials and hire hands.
ev.t_big_commission.borrow.success: Two sleepless years — and the work is done. It's shown to visitors, and you now have a workshop of your own with apprentices.
ev.t_big_commission.borrow.failure: Materials went up, workers drifted off, and the commission went to someone else. Only the debts remain.
ev.t_big_commission.partner: Take it on with your rival
ev.t_big_commission.partner.ok: You and your old rival split the work and the profit. Turns out you do better together than apart.
ev.t_big_commission.decline.ok: The commission went to another workshop. Safer — but in a couple of years you'll realize what you missed.
ev.t_commission_fame.title: A Master's Fame
ev.t_commission_fame.text: A distinguished traveler stood a long time before your work in the temple, then sought out your workshop. “I want the same — for my own city,” he said, and laid down a deposit that took your breath away.
ev.t_adoption.title: Another Man's Name
ev.t_adoption.text: A rich, childless old man you've done business with offers to adopt you and make you his heir. You'd take his name and enter his family, and in the eyes of the law your own father would no longer be your father. Your father doesn't know yet.
ev.t_adoption.text.athens: A rich, childless old man you've done business with offers to adopt you so that his line and his household altars won't die out. You'd join his house and his deme, receive his whole fortune — and leave your own father's family. Your father doesn't know yet.
ev.t_adoption.accept.ok: The rite is done, the name changed. You have a house with columns, slaves and fields. Your own father, when he heard, said nothing — he simply turned away.
ev.t_adoption.negotiate: Ask to keep ties with your own family
ev.t_adoption.negotiate.success: The old man thought it over and agreed: “Good that you don't forget your own.” You became his heir without losing your father.
ev.t_adoption.negotiate.failure: The old man took offense. “I need a son, not a guest.” A month later he adopted someone else.
ev.t_adoption.refuse.ok: You said you already have a father. When he heard, your father was lost for words for the first time you can remember.
ev.t_adoption_contest.title: The Nephews
ev.t_adoption_contest.text: Your adoptive father has died. His nephews, who waited all their lives for the inheritance, have gone to court: the adoption, they say, was a fraud, and the old man wasn't in his right mind.
ev.t_adoption_contest.court.success: Witnesses confirmed the old man was of sound mind. The court left everything to you and made the nephews pay the costs.
ev.t_adoption_contest.court.failure: The nephews found the right people. Half the inheritance went to them, and now you have a sworn enemy.
ev.t_adoption_contest.settle.ok: You set aside a share for them. The nephews left unhappy, but they've stopped suing.
ev.t_sycophant.title: The Sycophant
ev.t_sycophant.text: A man with an oily smile approaches you — a well-known sycophant. He has “happened to learn” that you supposedly spoke disrespectfully of the gods and hid part of your income. He's willing to forget it — for a fee. Otherwise it's court before hundreds of jurors.
ev.t_sycophant.note: In Athens “sycophants” were people who profited from denunciations and threats of prosecution: any citizen could bring a public charge, and this was used for extortion. There was a special lawsuit against sycophants, but fear of them is a constant theme in the speeches and comedies of the 5th–4th centuries BC.
ev.t_sycophant.pay.ok: He counted the coins and bowed. You hope never to see him again — but his kind always come back.
ev.t_sycophant.court: Hire a speechwriter and fight it
ev.t_sycophant.court.success: You learned the speech written for you by heart. The jurors laughed at the accuser and acquitted you by a huge majority.
ev.t_sycophant.court.failure: The jurors believed him, not you. A huge fine and disgrace before the whole city.
ev.t_sycophant.countersue.success: You dragged all his past extortions into the light. The court convicted him, and people call you the one who wasn't afraid.
ev.t_sycophant.countersue.failure: He had good witnesses, and yours had poor memories. You lost and paid for your boldness.
ev.t_sycophant.flee: Move to the countryside, far from the city
ev.t_sycophant.flee.ok: You moved to a village. Sycophants don't like dusty roads — but you can forget about your business in the city.
ev.t_sycophant_again.title: He's Back
ev.t_sycophant_again.text: The sycophant is at your door again, with the same smile. “Circumstances have changed. I need a little more.”
ev.t_sycophant_again.pay.ok: You paid. Now you know it will never end.
ev.t_sycophant_again.fight.success: You gathered his other victims, and together you beat him. He won't come to anyone's door again.
ev.t_sycophant_again.fight.failure: The court took his side again. You lost money; he lost nothing.
ev.t_games_victory.title: The Victor's Wreath
ev.t_games_victory.text: You won the footrace at the local games, and the whole city is talking about you. Your old trainer swears that with legs like yours you could win at Olympia: ten months of training, the journey to Elis, and eternal glory — or disgrace before all of Hellas.
ev.t_games_victory.text.athens: You won the footrace at the Panathenaia and took home an amphora of sacred oil. Your old trainer swears you could win at Olympia too — and Athens feeds an Olympic victor at public expense in the Prytaneion for the rest of his life. Or it's disgrace before all of Hellas.
ev.t_games_victory.text.egypt: You won the footrace at the Ptolemaia in Alexandria, and the whole city is talking about you. Your old trainer swears you could win at Olympia: Alexandrians have brought wreaths home from there before. Ten months of training, a voyage overseas — and eternal glory or disgrace.
ev.t_games_victory.olympia.success: You touched the finishing stone first. An olive wreath, your name cried by the herald — and at home they welcome you as a hero, as if you'd won a war.
ev.t_games_victory.olympia.failure: You came fourth. Olympia gives no prize for second place, let alone fourth — and you return home quietly.
ev.t_games_victory.hire_out: Compete for another city, for money
ev.t_games_victory.hire_out.ok: A rich city paid to have the herald announce you as theirs. Good money — but back home, they say, people want to tear down your statue.
ev.t_games_victory.settle.ok: You hung the wreath over the hearth. Every tavern in the quarter will pour you a free cup until you're old.
ev.t_victor_honors.title: The Statue
ev.t_victor_honors.text: The city has set up your bronze statue by the stadium — young, swift, a wreath on its head. Boys touch its knees for luck, and you, gray-haired now, come by to look at the man you were.
ev.t_hetaira.title: The Hetaira from Miletus
ev.t_hetaira.text: You've fallen in love with a hetaira from Miletus — educated, witty, a match for any philosopher in argument. But she isn't Athenian, and by law your children won't be citizens. Your father has already picked out a bride from a good family, with a dowry.
ev.t_hetaira.note: Under Pericles' law of 451 BC, only those with two Athenian parents could be citizens of Athens. Pericles himself lived with Aspasia of Miletus, and the Assembly made their son a citizen only as an exception, after Pericles' legitimate sons had died.
ev.t_hetaira.live_together.ok: She moved into your house, and it filled with guests, debates and laughter. Your father stopped visiting, and a character suspiciously like you has appeared in the comedies.
ev.t_hetaira.citizen_bride: Marry an Athenian, as your father wishes
ev.t_hetaira.citizen_bride.ok: The wedding went as it should. Your wife is quiet and kind. And sometimes you walk past a certain house without raising your eyes.
ev.t_hetaira.both.success: Your wife pretends not to know, the hetaira pretends not to be jealous. As long as everyone pretends, life is bearable.
ev.t_hetaira.both.failure: The secret came out at the very first banquet. Your father-in-law is furious, your wife silent for weeks, and the city laughs.
ev.t_hetaira_children.title: Illegitimate
ev.t_hetaira_children.text: {npc}, your child by the Milesian woman, has grown up, and now the full weight of the law comes down: {g=npc_sex:he isn't entered on the deme's roll of citizens|no citizen will take her as a wife}, and others jeer at {g=npc_sex:him|her} as a bastard. {npc} looks at you and waits to see what you'll do.
ev.t_hetaira_children.petition: Petition the Assembly for an exception
ev.t_hetaira_children.petition.success: The Assembly heard you out and voted: {npc} is Athenian. You wept on the Pnyx and weren't ashamed.
ev.t_hetaira_children.petition.failure: The Assembly refused. The law is the law, they said — even for those you love.
ev.t_hetaira_children.send_abroad: Send {g=npc_sex:him|her} to seek a fortune overseas
ev.t_hetaira_children.send_abroad.ok: You gave money and letters to friends in the colonies. There, nobody asks about your mother — they ask what you can do.
ev.t_hetaira_children.accept.ok: You said that's how the world is. {npc} nodded, but left without a word.
ev.t_epikleros.title: The Heiress
ev.t_epikleros.text: Your father has died leaving no sons. By law you're now an epikleros — an heiress who passes, together with the property, to the nearest male relative. Your father's cousin, twice your age, has already laid claim: to the land, the house — and to you. Even if you're married.
ev.t_epikleros.note: In Athens a daughter with no brothers became an epikleros: her nearest paternal kinsman could claim her in marriage along with the estate, and her existing marriage could be dissolved for it. The law aimed to keep property within the family; sons of such a marriage became their grandfather's heirs.
ev.t_epikleros.accept.ok: You entered your kinsman's house as his wife. Your father's land stayed in the family, and one day it will pass to your sons. It's the only thought that warms you.
ev.t_epikleros.dowry_deal: Persuade him to take the land and give you a dowry
ev.t_epikleros.dowry_deal.success: He thought it over and agreed: the land matters more to him than a young wife with a temper. You got a dowry and the freedom to choose.
ev.t_epikleros.dowry_deal.failure: He just laughed. A month later you entered his house as his wife — without consent and without joy.
ev.t_epikleros.fight: Fight for your marriage in court
ev.t_epikleros.fight.success: You and your husband proved the estate was small and the kinsman wanted only the land. The archon left you with your husband, and part of the property to you.
ev.t_epikleros.fight.failure: The archon ruled by the letter of the law. Your marriage is dissolved, and you pass to your kinsman along with your father's house.
ev.t_epikleros.flee.ok: You fled beyond the borders of Attica, leaving behind both the inheritance and your old name. Free — but in Athens they speak of you in whispers.
ev.t_delator.title: The Informer
ev.t_delator.text: At a dinner you made a careless joke about the emperor — everyone laughed. Three days later an informer charged you with treason against the majesty of the emperor. Cases like this end in exile or confiscation, and the informer gets a quarter of the convicted man's property.
ev.t_delator.note: Under the emperors, beginning with Tiberius, charges of maiestas (treason) became the weapon of informers — the delatores. By law the accuser received part of the convicted person's property, which turned denunciation into a profitable trade. Tacitus describes people tried for a careless word, a poem or a joke.
ev.t_delator.friend_at_court: Look for a protector at court
ev.t_delator.friend_at_court.success: An influential freedman of the emperor put in a word. The case was dropped, and the informer moved on to another victim.
ev.t_delator.friend_at_court.failure: The protector took the money and did nothing. The sentence: exile to an island and confiscation of half your property.
ev.t_delator.confess: Admit guilt and beg for mercy
ev.t_delator.confess.ok: You repented before the Senate, in tears. The emperor graciously settled for a heavy fine. Your friends now give you a wide berth.
ev.t_delator.counter.success: Your witnesses proved the joke had been twisted. The informer was convicted of slander, and you were awarded damages.
ev.t_delator.counter.failure: The countersuit was taken as insolence. The sentence: exile to an island and confiscation of most of your property.
ev.t_delator.retire: Withdraw to your estate and “fall ill”
ev.t_delator.retire.ok: You left for the Sabine hills and haven't shown your face in Rome. You've been forgotten — along with your business and your connections.
ev.t_exile_recall.title: Return from Exile
ev.t_exile_recall.text: A ship reached the island with news: the new emperor has pardoned those exiled under the old one. You return to Rome — older, but alive. Part of your property has even been returned.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.title: Proscriptions
ev.t_proscription_sulla.text: New lists have been posted in the Forum — and your name is on one. You were never Sulla's enemy, but one of his freedmen has taken a liking to your estate. The killer is promised a reward; your property will go to auction.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.note: In 82–81 BC the dictator Sulla published lists of the “proscribed”: they could be killed with impunity, a bounty was paid for their heads, and their property was auctioned. People were often added for the sake of their wealth — as in the case of Sextus Roscius, defended by the young Cicero.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.flee: Flee to the mountains at once
ev.t_proscription_sulla.flee.ok: You left that same night, in a slave's cloak, with a handful of coins. Others got your property, but you're alive.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.bribe.success: He took the money, and your name vanished from the lists as quietly as it appeared. You'll never know whose name went up in its place.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.bribe.failure: He took the money — and sent the killers. You fled through the garden, leaving everything.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.hide.success: A loyal slave brought you food in the tomb outside the city for a month. The storm passed, but the estate had already been plundered.
ev.t_proscription_sulla.hide.failure: You were betrayed. You tore free of the killers, wounded, and fled to the mountains, leaving everything you had.
ev.t_proscription_return.title: Amnesty
ev.t_proscription_return.text: Sulla has laid down his power, and fugitives are allowed to return. Your estate was sold off for a pittance long ago, and strangers live in it. You stand at the familiar gate, and not even the dog knows you.
ev.t_proscription_return.sue.success: The court ruled the sale unlawful. Part of your land came back to you — and your head spins as if after a long illness.
ev.t_proscription_return.sue.failure: The new owners are friends of powerful men. The case dragged on and came to nothing.
ev.t_proscription_return.start_over.ok: You rented a room in Rome and started from nothing. Sometimes that's easier than forever looking back.
ev.t_proscribed_master.title: The Master on the Lists
ev.t_proscribed_master.text: Your master's name is on the triumvirs' proscription lists. Heralds cry at every crossroads: a slave who betrays a proscribed man will get freedom, citizenship and a fortune. The master is hiding in the house, and only you know where.
ev.t_proscribed_master.note: In 43 BC Antony, Octavian and Lepidus declared proscriptions in which Cicero, among many others, died. A slave who betrayed his master was promised freedom, citizenship and a large reward. Appian tells of betrayals — and of slaves who hid their masters and even sacrificed themselves for them.
ev.t_proscribed_master.betray.ok: You showed the soldiers the way. The reward was paid in full: you're free and rich. Only at night you dream of that door creaking.
ev.t_proscribed_master.hide_master.succe: You got the master out of the city disguised as a porter and saw him onto a ship. When the storm passed he came back, and the first thing he did was set you free — with words you'll remember forever.
ev.t_proscribed_master.hide_master.failu: The soldiers found the hiding place. They took the master away, and beat you half to death for hiding him.
ev.t_proscribed_master.stay_out.ok: You pretended to know nothing. One morning the master was simply gone. What became of him, no one knows.
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.title: The Master's Son
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.text: After the amnesty the son of the man you once betrayed returned to Rome. He found you in your shop and silently laid an old key on the counter — the key to that very house.
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.beg.success: He was silent a long time, then said, “Back then everyone was saving their own skin.” And left. You feel lighter — a little.
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.beg.failure: He wouldn't listen. A month later your shop was wrecked, and the whole quarter calls you nothing but “the one who sold his master.”
ev.t_betrayal_haunts.leave.ok: You sold the shop in a hurry and moved to the port of Ostia. No one there knows who you are.
ev.t_land_confiscation.title: The Surveyors
ev.t_land_confiscation.text: Surveyors have come with poles and boundary stones: your district's land is being given to veterans. Your plot, where your ancestors' bones lie, goes to a former centurion — he's already been round to look, nodding approvingly.
ev.t_land_confiscation.note: In the 1st century BC generals paid their veterans in land: Sulla, Caesar and the triumvirs confiscated plots from Italian communities. The poet Virgil mourned such evictions in his Eclogues; according to tradition he managed to recover his own farm through Octavian's intervention.
ev.t_land_confiscation.plead: Go to Rome and plead for protection
ev.t_land_confiscation.plead.success: An influential man liked your bluntness. Your plot was struck off the lists — the centurion will get another.
ev.t_land_confiscation.plead.failure: You spent a month knocking on doors in Rome for nothing. When you got back, a stranger was on your field. You had to move to the city.
ev.t_land_confiscation.tenant: Stay on as the new owner's tenant
ev.t_land_confiscation.tenant.ok: You plow the same land — only now you hand half the harvest to a man who knows nothing about farming.
ev.t_land_confiscation.city: Take what they offer and go to Rome
ev.t_land_confiscation.city.ok: You loaded your belongings on a cart and went to Rome, where thousands like you look for day labor.
ev.t_land_confiscation.resist.success: The neighbors stood with you, and the veterans decided there was easier land to be had. They left you alone.
ev.t_land_confiscation.resist.failure: The veterans had fought for twenty years; you hadn't fought a day. They beat you and drove you off, and you reached Rome empty-handed.
ev.t_land_veteran.title: The Old Centurion
ev.t_land_veteran.text: The centurion who got your land has grown old, and he has no heirs. One evening he came to you himself. “The land is weeping without you. I don't know how to work it. Let's make a deal.”
ev.t_land_veteran.buy_back.ok: You gave everything you'd saved — and you stand on your own land as its master again. You plow the first furrow slowly, like a prayer.
ev.t_land_veteran.befriend.ok: You teach him to plow; he tells you about his wars. A strange friendship — but a strong one.
ev.t_land_veteran.refuse.ok: You said you don't buy what was stolen from you. The centurion nodded and left.
ev.t_province_governor.title: The Province
ev.t_province_governor.text: The lot has given you a province — for a year you'll be its governor, with lictors, troops and power over life and death. The elections cost you a fortune, and your creditors hint transparently: one is expected to come back from a province rich.
ev.t_province_governor.note: Governors of Roman provinces held nearly unlimited power and often enriched themselves at the provincials' expense. A special court existed for extortion cases; the most famous trial was Cicero's prosecution of Verres, governor of Sicily, in 70 BC. Verres went into exile without waiting for the verdict.
ev.t_province_governor.squeeze.ok: You came back with chests of silver, statues from other people's temples, and your debts paid in full. The provincials curse your name — in whispers, for now.
ev.t_province_governor.honest.ok: You judged fairly and took no gifts. You brought back almost no money, but the provincials walked you all the way to your ship.
ev.t_province_governor.decline.ok: You stayed in Rome. Your creditors are unhappy, the senators surprised, and your wife delighted.
ev.t_repetundae.title: The Extortion Trial
ev.t_repetundae.text: The provincials sent an embassy to Rome, and an ambitious young orator has charged you with extortion. He's gathered mountains of evidence, and the whole Forum is talking about the trial.
ev.t_repetundae.advocate.success: Your advocate tangled the witnesses and moved the judges. Acquitted — though everyone knows how things really were.
ev.t_repetundae.advocate.failure: Even the best advocate couldn't save you. You're convicted, and there's only one thing left — exile.
ev.t_repetundae.exile.ok: You left before the verdict, taking what you could save. One can live in exile too — if one has money.
ev.t_repetundae.bribe_jury.success: A few purses passed at night did their work. Acquitted by a majority of two votes.
ev.t_repetundae.bribe_jury.failure: The bribery came to light. Now a new charge has been added to extortion, and you flee Rome.
ev.t_province_gratitude.title: Patron of a Province
ev.t_province_gratitude.text: An embassy has arrived from the province you once governed honestly: the city has chosen you as its patron, set up your statue in the agora, and sent gifts. An honest man can only dream of such a thing.
ev.t_charioteer.title: The Charioteer
ev.t_charioteer.text: A trainer for the Greens saw how you handle horses and wants to buy you for the circus. Charioteers die on the turns of the Circus Maximus, but the best of them are richer than senators, and all Rome knows their names.
ev.t_charioteer.note: Chariot racing in the Circus Maximus was Rome's great passion. Drivers, often slaves or freedmen, raced for the factions — Greens, Blues, Whites and Reds. The famous Gaius Appuleius Diocles won more than 1,400 races in the 2nd century AD and earned an enormous fortune.
ev.t_charioteer.race.success: You took the turn so close to the post that the stands gasped, and crossed the line first. A hundred thousand throats are shouting your name.
ev.t_charioteer.race.failure: On the seventh lap the chariot overturned. You survived, but you lay injured a long time, and the limp stayed.
ev.t_charioteer.bargain: Demand a share of the prizes
ev.t_charioteer.bargain.success: The trainer grumbled but agreed: part of the prize money goes into your peculium. Now you're racing for your freedom too.
ev.t_charioteer.bargain.failure: The trainer spat and bought someone else. Your master didn't forgive you for haggling.
ev.t_charioteer.stay.ok: You stayed with your master's horses. Safer — and quieter than the roar of the circus.
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.title: Darling of the Circus
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.text: After another victory the stands chanted “Freedom!” until the giver of the games nodded. Your master was paid, and you're free. What comes next is up to you.
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.keep_racing.ok: You signed with the faction as a free man. The prizes are yours now — all of them.
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.tavern: Buy a tavern by the circus
ev.t_charioteer_freedom.tavern.ok: You bought a tavern by the circus gates. Fans come in droves to drink with a living legend.
ev.t_love_gladiator.title: The Gladiator
ev.t_love_gladiator.text: You've lost your head over a gladiator — the one whose name is scrawled on the walls and who half the women of Rome sigh over. He wants you to run away with him to Capua. For a woman of your standing such an affair is a disgrace — and if it comes out, a trial and exile.
ev.t_love_gladiator.run_away.ok: You left it all — home, name, money — and went with him to Capua. In Rome they talk about you on every corner. You don't care.
ev.t_love_gladiator.secret.success: No one knows a thing. Your life has split in two, and the second half is the most alive.
ev.t_love_gladiator.secret.failure: A maid let it slip. A scandal across the city, divorce and disgrace — and a gladiator who didn't even come.
ev.t_love_gladiator.end.ok: You don't go to the amphitheater anymore. Sometimes, hearing his name, you leave the room.
ev.t_gladiator_falls.title: The Last Fight
ev.t_gladiator_falls.text: News came from the amphitheater: he fell in the arena. The crowd called for mercy, but the giver of the games gave no sign. You're alone in a strange city.
ev.t_gladiator_falls.go_home.ok: Your family took you back — with sighs, and without reproaches spoken aloud. Rome forgave the scandal faster than you forgave yourself.
ev.t_gladiator_falls.stay.ok: His comrades from the school took up a collection for you. You stayed in Capua — here at least they remember his name.
ev.t_nexum.title: Debt Bondage
ev.t_nexum.text: The bad harvest has eaten all your stores. The patrician moneylender will give grain and money only under nexum: if you don't repay on time, you'll work off the debt in his house — in chains, if he chooses. The children are hungry, and he's in no hurry.
ev.t_nexum.note: The early Roman Republic knew nexum — debt bondage in which the debtor pledged his own person and could be put in chains by the creditor. According to tradition it was abolished by the Lex Poetelia around 326 BC, after plebeian anger reached a breaking point. The details come mainly from Livy.
ev.t_nexum.bind.ok: You swore before witnesses with bronze and scales. There's grain, the children are fed. And the deadline is already dripping away like a water clock.
ev.t_nexum.sell_land.ok: You sold your father's plot to a patrician neighbor. Now you're free — and you hire yourself out to him as a day laborer.
ev.t_nexum.colony: Sign up for a new colony
ev.t_nexum.colony.ok: Rome is founding a colony on conquered land, and the settlers get plots. You leave with your family and a hundred others like you — to start from nothing on the frontier.
ev.t_nexum.clan_patron: Ask your clan's patron for help
ev.t_nexum.clan_patron.success: The patron helped with grain, no bondage — in exchange for loyalty and your vote in the assembly. That's a chain too, but a softer one.
ev.t_nexum.clan_patron.failure: The patron was busy with his own affairs and wouldn't even see you. You went home with nothing.
ev.t_nexum_end.title: The Debt Falls Due
ev.t_nexum_end.text: The term of the debt has run out, and there's no money. The moneylender has come with men and chains: by law you now belong to him until you've worked it off.
ev.t_nexum_end.pay.ok: You scraped together every last coin. The chains stayed with the moneylender, and you stayed home.
ev.t_nexum_end.work_off: Work it off in his house
ev.t_nexum_end.work_off.ok: For two years you worked in his house like a slave and slept in the stocks. You came out free — but a different person.
ev.t_nexum_end.tribunes: Appeal to the tribunes of the plebs
ev.t_nexum_end.tribunes.success: You showed the crowd in the Forum the scars from the chains. The plebs roared, the tribunes intervened, and the moneylender backed down.
ev.t_nexum_end.tribunes.failure: The tribunes listened but couldn't help. The moneylender took you away, and freedom was a long way off.
ev.t_monsoon_india.title: The Wind to India
ev.t_monsoon_india.text: Pilots know the secret: in summer the wind blows east off the sea so steadily that a ship from the Red Sea ports reaches India in forty days — and comes back on the winter wind with pepper, pearls and silk. One voyage can make you rich — or you may never return.
ev.t_monsoon_india.note: Around the end of the 2nd century BC Greek sailors learned to use the monsoon winds to cross the open sea from Egypt to India. Ships sailed from Berenice and Myos Hormos to Muziris and other ports; the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (1st century AD) describes the route, and Pliny complains of how much Roman gold flowed east.
ev.t_monsoon_india.go.success: A year later you returned to Alexandria sunburned, with sacks of pepper and stories of elephants and temples. The goods sold for five times the price. You're rich now.
ev.t_monsoon_india.go.failure: The ship lost its mast off Arabia. You returned nearly two years later, sick and empty-handed.
ev.t_monsoon_india.invest.success: The ship came back, and your share of the pepper brought in more than you'd earned in years.
ev.t_monsoon_india.invest.failure: The ship never returned. People say all sorts of things about it, but talk won't bring the money back.
ev.t_monsoon_india.stay.ok: You watched the sails go. Some will return rich; some won't return at all.
ev.t_india_friend.title: A Guest from Muziris
ev.t_india_friend.text: In Alexandria's harbor an Indian merchant sought you out — you once drank wine together on the Malabar coast. He's brought a shipload of spices and proposes a deal: his goods, your connections.
ev.t_india_friend.partner.success: The spices sold within a month. You swore to each other by all your gods and planned a new voyage.
ev.t_india_friend.partner.failure: Customs took a quarter of the value in duty, and the warehouse got damp. You split the loss evenly — as friends.
ev.t_india_friend.decline.ok: You drank to old times, and he sailed off with another partner.
ev.t_anachoresis.title: Fleeing the Taxes
ev.t_anachoresis.text: There's no way to pay this year's tax, and the collector has already promised debtors' prison. Two neighbors vanished last month — gone to the Delta marshes, where the reeds are taller than a man and officials never go. The old folk say people did the same under the pharaohs.
ev.t_anachoresis.note: Peasants fleeing their villages — anachoresis in Greek — was a common response to heavy taxes and compulsory labor in Ptolemaic and Roman Egypt. Fugitives hid in the Delta marshes, in temples with the right of asylum, or in other districts. The authorities alternately punished them and proclaimed pardons: a decree of 118 BC, for example, allowed fugitives to return without penalty.
ev.t_anachoresis.flee.ok: You slipped away at night by boat down the canal. Other fugitives live in the reeds: they cut papyrus, catch fish and pay nobody.
ev.t_anachoresis.asylum: Take refuge in a temple with right of asylum
ev.t_anachoresis.asylum.success: The priests let you inside the precinct wall, where collectors may not go. You'll wait here until the storm blows over.
ev.t_anachoresis.asylum.failure: The guards dragged you out of the temple courtyard despite the priests' shouts. Debtors' prison, and an inventory of everything you own.
ev.t_anachoresis.endure.ok: You did your time in debtors' prison and your belongings were auctioned. You came out sick and poor — but in your own village.
ev.t_anachoresis.bribe.success: The collector took the money and listed you as “without means.” You're safe for a year.
ev.t_anachoresis.bribe.failure: The collector took the money — and seized your property anyway. There's no one to complain to.
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.title: A Decree of Pardon
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.text: Word has reached the marshes: a decree has been posted — fugitives may return to their villages, and the debts of past years are forgiven. Some are already readying boats; others don't believe a word the officials say.
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.return.ok: You returned to your kin, and the village scribe wrote you back onto the rolls. The decree didn't lie — this time.
ev.t_anachoresis_amnesty.stay_marsh.ok: Here you've learned to weave papyrus mats and bow to no one. You have no wish to go back under someone else's rule.
ev.t_auxilia.title: Twenty-Five Years
ev.t_auxilia.text: Roman recruiters have come to the village. An auxiliary cohort or the fleet: twenty-five years of service, and then Roman citizenship, a bronze tablet with your name, and money for your old age. Your mother is crying and holding your hand.
ev.t_auxilia.note: Provincials, Egyptians among them, served in Rome's auxiliary forces and fleet. After 25–26 years of service a veteran received Roman citizenship, confirmed by a bronze “military diploma.” Many veterans settled in Egypt — for example at Karanis in the Fayum — and became prosperous landowners.
ev.t_auxilia.cohort.ok: They gave you a shield, a spear and a new Roman name for the rolls. Ahead: desert, garrisons and a quarter century of service.
ev.t_auxilia.fleet.ok: They sent you to a ship. You knew the Nile; now you'll learn the sea — for the next twenty-five years.
ev.t_auxilia.refuse.ok: You stayed in the village. Your mother stopped crying, and the recruiters moved on to the neighbors.
ev.t_auxilia_discharge.title: The Bronze Tablet
ev.t_auxilia_discharge.text: A quarter century is behind you. You've been handed a bronze tablet: from now on you're a Roman citizen, and so are your children. With your discharge money you buy land in the Fayum, where other veterans live, and the peasant neighbors bow to you in the street.
